title: Order in ‘the dark forest’: private resolution of a market failure
description: MEV extraction on Ethereum has exceeded $1 billion since 2020. This predatory environment, ‘the dark forest’, is permitted by code and legally ambiguous, but has been widely recognised by the community as a market failure. Standard welfare-economic accounts treat such failures as grounds for state intervention. Yet Ethereum’s social layer developed private mechanisms, chiefly proposer-builder separation and MEV-protected routing, that now handle over 90% of transaction volume. The talk offers three arguments. First, self-governance emerged where its canonical preconditions are absent, in a dispersed, pseudonymous community. Second, the case continues a lineage of financial self-regulation, notably the Chicago Board of Trade, which made private rules against manipulation decades before federal law. Third, private ordering has limits: these mechanisms also concentrated block building and remain sensitive to state sanctions, suggesting private orders develop in 'the shadow of the state'.
